Welcome from the
Head Teacher
Luckington School is an incredibly special place. We are a small school in the beautiful southern Cotswolds within travelling distance of Malmesbury and Chippenham. We offer a warm, welcoming and inclusive environment.
Although small, we pride ourselves on being global looking. We believe that our children have the potential to be the leaders and innovators of the future. Our school is extremely well resourced, thanks to a highly dedicated Friends Of Luckington School. All of our children have access to IT equipment to enrich and enhance their learning, which we believe to be crucial for life in today's society. To set them on their way, we provide a rich curriculum that prepares them for life in an ever changing world. This is underpinned by a set of 7 key values:
Resilience, Compassion, Honesty, Respect, Forgiveness, Reflectiveness and Positivity.

British Values
At Luckington Community School, we develop and promote British Values throughout our school and within our curriculum.
A key part of our plan for education is to ensure children become valuable and fully rounded members of society who treat others with respect and leave school fully prepared for life in modern Britain.
British Values
Tolerance for those of different faiths and beliefs
To do this our children will develop;
An understanding of how citizens can influence decision-making through the democratic process
An understanding that the freedom to hold other faiths and beliefs is protected in law
An acceptance that people having different faiths and beliefs to oneself (or having none) should be accepted and tolerated, and should not be the cause of discriminatory behaviour
An understanding of the importance or identifying and combating discrimination
The mission statement and aims of the school clearly reflect these values, and the whole school strives to uphold them.
Below you can find a more detailed summary of British Values in our school.

Welcome from the Headteacher
Welcome to Luckington Community School!
Welcome and thank you for visiting our website.
Luckington School is an incredibly special place. We are a small school in the beautiful southern Cotswolds within travelling distance of Malmesbury and Chippenham. We offer a warm, welcoming and inclusive environment.
Although small, we pride ourselves on being global looking. We believe that our children have the potential to be the leaders and innovators of the future. Our school is extremely well resourced, thanks to a highly dedicated Friends Of Luckington School. All of our children have access to IT equipment to enrich and enhance their learning, which we believe to be crucial for life in today's society. To set them on their way, we provide a rich curriculum that prepares them for life in an ever changing world. This is underpinned by a set of 7 key values:
Resilience, Compassion, Honesty, Respect, Forgiveness, Reflectiveness and Positivity.
If you would like to know more about our school and find out how we manage mixed ages in our classes, then you are very welcome to come and visit. I would love to show you around. The children of Luckington very much enjoy sharing their achievements and successes. You will see how supportive they are of each other and how engaged with their learning they are. As our children work closely with other year groups as soon as they start school, we find that our children transition extremely well into Key Stage 1 from Early Years, into Key Stage 2 from Key Stage 1 and onwards into Key Stage 3 and secondary school.
We regularly compete and participate in wider events relating to sport and drama. We include visits and visitors that enrich our curriculum beyond National Curriculum expectations. Our after school club offer is excellent, with many of these being either subsidised or free. These clubs vary according to the season and cater for a range of interests, including sport, gardening, cooking and French.
We hope that you enjoy your visit to our website, and that you find any information you are looking for.
Thank you, and I do hope to meet you soon.
Mrs Julie Gingell (Headteacher)

Our Values
It is our aim to guide our children towards being happy and productive members of their local, national, global and online communities when they grow up. Skills and knowledge are a very important part of this, but are underpinned by having a set of strong values on which they can make positive decisions about their lives.
We consulted with our community on which 'values' we see as the most important. Our values are intrinsically linked to the British Values:
Each week we have assemblies on our school values and our British Values. We also have singing assembly and a celebration assembly, which we call 'Stars assembly' to which parents are invited too.

Personal, Social and Health Education and Relationships and Sex Education
At Luckington our objective with PSHE is to make ensure that all children are knowledgeable, rational and empathic. Through RSE, we aim to ensure that all children are knowledgeable and develop a mature approach towards making decisions in their personal lives.
As a child grows, so does their independence. Along with this independence comes more responsibility. We want to ensure that our children are equipped with the values and skills they need as they grow.
We teach PSHE/RSE weekly, but there are always strong links to the area through our weekly assemblies, particularly when we are looking at our school values. Whenever needed, we use additional sessions throughout the week to respond to any things that have come up that need to be addressed. We use Coram SCARF scheme to deliver the PSHE curriculum. Coram Life Education and SCARF is the UK's leading charity provider of PSHE and wellbeing education in primary schools. SCARF stands for; Safety, Caring, Achievement, Resilience and Friendship.
It is important that our curriculum in this area stays relevant, reflecting the times that we live in. We therefore subscribe to the PSHE Association who keep us up to date.
To enrich this further and to highlight key messages further, we work closely with the NSPCC, Stay Safe Initiative and the Life Education Bus.

Music
"Without music, life would be a mistake."
Friedrich Nietzche
Our aim in music is to ensure that all children develop interest and enjoyment in music.
The benefits of music are great. It is not only an enjoyable pass time (or perhaps career!), but it can also be a very sociable interest, mentally stimulating and at other times relaxing. It is important to us that our children are able to experience music in all shapes and forms.
Each week the children take part in a music lesson and singing lesson in school. We also access the Wiltshire Music service so many of our children receive individual instrumental lessons. To bolster this further we take up every enrichment opportunity we can; whether that's the school choir, a trip to Young Voices or an opera workshop, there's always something musical going on!
Curriculum Subjects
Music

Art
"Every human is an artist."
Don Miguel Ruiz
Over their time at Luckington, we aim to ensure that all children develop their ability to express themselves creatively through a range of media.
We not only believe that art is natural way for people to express themselves and communicate, we also see it as an effective tool in maintaining positive mental health. Our aim is to give the children experience in creating art in as many different media and styles as possible not only so they can develop their skills, but also to help them find that 'spark'. Art is not just about drawing or painting; it's about being able to express yourself and that can be done in a number of ways.
At Luckington, we believe art is best taught in 'blocks'. Therefore, every term the children will do an art topic, but it is often done in a series of afternoons over the space of a week or two. We have chosen this approach because we feel that the children can become fully immersed in a topic, rather than having a series of short, disjointed lessons.
Curriculum Subjects
Art

Computing
To access our IT curriculum Purple Mash at home, use this link
"Alan Turing gave us a mathematical model of digital computing that has completely withstood the test of time. He gave us a very, very clear description that was truly prophetic."
George Dyson
In our school, our Computing curriculum is designed to make sure that every child has the skills and knowledge to use technology creatively, safely and innovatively.
There has been a significant shift over the past decade in terms of technological advances that affect everyday life. Our children can intuitively use programs and apps from a young age, therefore, the key to our curriculum is to give them the skills to be creative.
It is also important that our curriculum teaches the children to stay safe online. Internet safety runs throughout our Computing curriculum but it also runs throughout the wider curriculum, particularly in PSHE and RE. It is our belief that online safety is a life skill, comparable to road safety or water safety.
Curriculum Subjects
Computing

Design Technology
"Good buildings come from good people and all problems are solved by good design."
Stephen Gardiner
At Luckington, our main objective through DT is to ensure that all children are innovative, forward-thinking, and can plan and reflect effectively. Many of the skills taught in DT can be applied across the curriculum: planning, reflection and research to name but a few.
Much like with art, we believe DT is best taught in 'blocks'. Therefore, every term the children will do a DT topic, but it is often done in a series of afternoons over the space of a week or two. We have chosen this approach because we feel that the children can become fully immersed in a topic, rather than having a series of short, disjointed lessons.
Curriculum Subjects
Design Technology

English
"When I read great literature, great drama, speeches or sermons, I feel that the human mind has not achieved anything greater than the ability to share feelings and thoughts through language."
James Earl Jones
At Luckington, our aim is to ensure that all children are strong, confident readers, who read for pleasure and for knowledge and can communicate clearly, eloquently and skilfully using written language.
In both classes English is taught every day through a mix of specific English lessons, guided reading, handwriting, phonics and spelling. We believe in a cross-curricular approach to teaching English so you will find a great deal of reading and writing being done in other subjects.
To deliver our phonics and reading curriculum we use the 'Unlocking Letters and Sounds' phonics Scheme. Please see the document below for more information.
Please see the powerpoint below of our parents information session.
Curriculum Subjects

French
"You live a new life for every language you speak. If you only know one language, you only live once."
Czech Proverb
We feel that is vital to ensure that all children have the key knowledge and skills in a language other than English. A second (or third, or fourth!) language is an amazing skill to have and can open up a great deal of further opportunities.
French is a language that we know the children can take on and develop when they move to secondary school; giving them the basis to branch out to more languages should they wish. We teach it once a week in Class 2. In Class 1, the children regularly practise common French words and phrases and also have the opportunity to take part in an after school French club.
French Skills and Knowledge Progression 2020
Curriculum Subjects

Geography
"You can travel the seas, poles and deserts and see nothing. To really understand the world, you need to get under the skin of the people and places. In other words, learn about geography!"
Michael Palin
Through geography we wish to ensure that all children develop a strong understanding of the physical and cultural differences and similarities between our locality and other places in the UK and the world.
The concept of community is more important now than ever. Since the pandemic we have seen the power of strong communities and we want our pupils to be positive and productive members of the communities they are part of: local, national, online and international. Part of this is understanding the world around them; the differences and similarities between everyone on the planet.
Geography is taught discreetly as a topic once a year, but elements of the subject are touched on across the curriculum. For example, the geographical links to a particular artist may be examined in art. We also 'drip feed' as much geography and history as we can through assemblies, using the marvellous world map in our hall.
Curriculum Subjects
Geography

History
"A people without the knowledge of their past history, origin and culture is like a tree without roots."
Marcus Garvey
Through our history curriculum we aim to ensure that all children develop an understanding of how what has happened in the past affects the present and the future.
We teach a discreet history topic once a year but embrace elements of the subject in other curricular areas where possible. For example, if we were looking at the geography of the local area, knowledge of nearby Roman settlements would be an integral part of the learning. Our local area is steeped in history and we like to base topics around it when we can.
Curriculum Subjects

Mathematics
"Pure mathematics is, in its way, the poetry of logical ideas."
Albert Einstein
At Luckington we aim to ensure that all children have mastered the key mathematical skills and concepts and have the ability to reason mathematically.
We all know the importance of ensuring learning is embedded in your child's long term memory. Therefore, to address this, we teach maths using an approach called 'Maths Mastery'. Teaching maths for mastery is a transformational approach to maths teaching which stems from high performing Asian nations such as Singapore. When taught to master maths, children develop their mathematical fluency without resorting to rote learning and are able to solve non-routine maths problems without having to memorise procedures.
You can find out more information about how we teach maths in our maths policy which you can download below. To get an idea of the content of our maths curriculum, download the Skills and Knowledge Progression.
